messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1843212345 — elevated p99 latency for /v1/stream in us-west-2, automatic paging triggered. p95 ~ 180ms -> 420ms, p99 ~ 520ms -> 3.2s. Error rate stable. Impact: streaming sessions stall (clients see long response gaps). Paging oncall: @amanda (oncall)
amanda (oncall): grabbing it, looking at dashboards now. thanks.
li (eng-sre): I see pager, fs utilization and gpu metrics look fine. KV cache miss spikes around the same time as the p99 jump.
carla (support): we have 3 customers who opened support threads about streaming stalls, one customer reported partial transcript delays and another reported client reconnects. Marking potential customer impact high.
amanda (oncall): ok marking P1, calling runtime. @ravi can you join?
ravi (runtime): on it. initial hypothesis: continuous-batching path is packing long and short sequences together and causing stray big-kv evictions and scheduling unfairness => streaming stalls. seeing queue depth variance in batcher logs.
marcus (eng-mgr): if we need a quick mitigation, consider reducing max batch size or enabling pack-shed mode. priority is to restore streaming responsiveness for customers.
amanda (oncall): agreed. before we change anything — what's the safest quick revert? fallback to model-variant with lower memory footprint?
ravi (runtime): yes we can route streaming to rw-medium-v2-quant fallback across the pool for this tier; cheaper but faster. Also change batcher config `max_batch_size` down and bump fairness weight for streaming buckets. I'll prepare both.
li (eng-sre): creating a live mitigation playbook entry, will coordinate infra changes.
carla (support): I'll notify the affected customers that we're investigating and may toggle routing to a lower-latency variant.
amanda (oncall): make the change and post commands here before you run them so deploy-bot can record.
deploy-bot: queued action: validate/approve required for runtime config changes.
ravi (runtime): posting proposed low-risk actions —
```
# quick mitigations (safe, non-destructive)
1) route streaming requests in us-west-2 for prod-tier to rw-medium-v2-quant (canary to 100% if OK)
2) reduce continuous-batcher.max_batch_size: 32 -> 8
3) enable stream_bucket.fairness_weight: 0.5 -> 1.5
```
I'll do 1) first then 2) if latency doesn't improve.
li (eng-sre): monitoring signals to watch: p95/p99, streaming idle gaps (ms), kv_cache_miss_rate, batch_size_histogram, scheduler_queue_hold_time.
amanda (oncall): go for 1) now. please paste the routing change command.
ravi (runtime): running the routing flip now — command below (dry-run validated):
```
POST /admin/routing
{
  "region":"us-west-2",
  "route_filter":"/v1/stream",
  "traffic_percent":100,
  "target_model":"rw-medium-v2-quant",
  "note":"emergency streaming fallback to reduce tail latency"
}
```
deploy-bot: action started by ravi; ETA ~15s for propagation. :rocket:
li (eng-sre): seeing p99 drop at edge (first hop) to ~1.0s, p95 now ~250ms. kv_cache_miss rate still elevated but batch tail effects reduced.
carla (support): sending customer update: "We've routed streaming traffic to a lower-latency model variant while we investigate root cause; no data loss expected, responses slightly shorter in tokenization in rare cases."
amanda (oncall): good. hold for 10m to confirm.
(10 minutes pass)
li (eng-sre): after 10m: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~680ms -> significantly better than 3.2s. However occasional 2-3s spikes persist correlated with batch pack sizes >16. Batch histogram shows a long tail.
ravi (runtime): next low-risk step: drop max_batch_size to 8 in continuous-batcher config. here's dry-run change:
```
PATCH /admin/continuous-batcher/config
{
  "region":"us-west-2",
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "pack_timeout_ms": 8
}
```
li (eng-sre): warn — this may increase per-token cost slightly but should reduce stray long-running batches and preemption.
amanda (oncall): do it once ravi confirms. also capture logs for a 30s window afterwards.
ravi (runtime): applying patch now.
deploy-bot: config-patch applied by ravi at 1843212700; rollout to 100% in us-west-2.
li (eng-sre): immediate improvement: p99 down to 420-500ms, p95 180-240ms. streaming stall reports dropping. batch_size_histogram now capped around 8-10 (some padding), scheduler queue_hold_time reduced.
marcus (eng-mgr): nice. any remaining customer impact?
carla (support): two customers still reporting occasional stalls but less frequent. I recommended retry/backoff in client and escalated to the platform team for per-customer routing if needed.
amanda (oncall): ok, next root-cause steps while mitigation remains in place: collect traces for mixed sequence-length sessions, KV eviction patterns, and scheduler fairness math. Ravi, Li — assign follow-ups and set a timeline.
ravi (runtime): taking RCAs: will instrument batcher to tag per-batch max_seq_len, kv_eviction_count, and scheduling decisions for a 6h window. expected analysis in 48h. Will also prototype weighted packing where short streams prefer their own buckets.
li (eng-sre): I'll correlate with KV cache metrics and paging events from node-exporter; will check if memory pressure or GC on runtime threads contributed. 24-48h timeline for a full hypothesis.
marcus (eng-mgr): assign postmortem owner: ravi, write up impact, timeline, and long-term fix options (pack isolation, adaptive batch caps, per-tenant routing).
amanda (oncall): thanks team. I'll close the pager if we keep p99 < 700ms for 1h and customer-reported stalls drop to near zero.
carla (support): I'll run customer follow-ups and reopen if any regression.
(ITERATION)
li (eng-sre): note: we also found one service periodically emitting an out-of-band large request that inflated batch packing windows — created ticket ENG-8821 to rate-limit that path.
marcus (eng-mgr): good catch. add to postmortem and link to the mitigation (batch cap).
(closure after 1h)
amanda (oncall): closing pager. summary: emergency fallback to rw-medium-v2-quant + reduce continuous-batcher.max_batch_size to 8 restored streaming latency to acceptable levels. Customers notified. Postmortem assigned to ravi; incident severity P2 (customer-facing but mitigated).
ravi (runtime): postmortem plan: timeline, metrics, root-cause (mixed sequence lengths + opportunistic large requests causing packing amplification), short-term fixes (batch cap, fairness weight), medium-term (pack isolation + adaptive batch cap), long-term (model routing/class-based QoS).
carla (support): I'll update customer incidents and add the language about mitigations and expected follow-up ETA 48h for technical postmortem.
deploy-bot: incident 1843212345 marked resolved by amanda at 1843212967. :white_check_mark:
marcus (eng-mgr): great job everyone. continuous-batcher follow-up ticket and postmortem assigned; please include cost delta analysis for the batch cap change.
(END OF THREAD)
